messages.subject: Problem with stacked density plot
parts:
Hello!

I am having trouble producing a stacked density plot. I always get
"Error in pairwise(nseq)..." shown below, even for other data sets.
The equivalent notation using ggplot and geom_density leads to the
same error. What am I doing wrong?

Example:
library(ggplot2)
qplot(mpg, ..density.., data=mtcars, geom="density", fill=factor(mtcars
$gear), position="stack")
Error in pairwise(nseq) :
pairwise: N must be positve numeric and of length 1
In addition: Warning message:
In if ((c == ".") | (c == "-")) { :
the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

Thanks,

Eckart

messages.author: ee4c267570e4e155
messages.subject: Re: Problem with stacked density plot
parts:
Ok, I am closer to the solution:
If I only load the ggplot2 library, things work fine, without error
and as advertised! If I, however, load in my self-written library with
its dependencies first, several conflicts appear upon reading the
ggplot2 library. So my error seems to be an issue with name conflicts
and overwritten function definitions. Being a pragmatist, I now write
out the result table from my own analysis to a file, restart R, read
that table back in a load ggplot2. This workaround does the trick.
Any great suggestions though for resolving name conflicts between
libraries or do I have to stick to my workaround?

Eckart
